Aperio Space Technologies GmbH develops key technologies and software for resilient, secure, and scalable satellite networks with a platform-independent approach. With a patent-pending method for dynamically determining network topology and operating multi-orbit and multi-platform satellite networks, Aperio enables operators to access their satellites in real time to retrieve data and perform continuous operations. After joining the Aperio network, satellites will be able to downlink more data faster, thereby increasing mission returns. This is particularly crucial in earth observation, where the instant availability of large amounts of data is critical for applications such as disaster response, environmental monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, cargo monitoring, and surveillance.
Through intelligent dynamic routing, the data traffic in future telecommunication networks that (even partly) rely on satellites will be optimized and secured with advanced cryptographic mechanisms that Aperio integrates into their protocols. At the same time, space will become safer through Aperio’s work. Not only does the dynamic topology eliminate single points of failure and make telecommunication and earth observation constellations much more resilient, but it also enables instant manoeuvring for collision avoidance and autonomous operations, which will become mandatory given the exponential rise of active satellites in orbit.

description: The University of Huelva (UHU) is a young, public university, striving for excellence and fully implicated in the academic and professional future of its more than 12.000 students. entityDescription:
Finapp has designed and patented the next generation of CRNS probes that use cosmic rays to measure water into the soil and snow non-invasively, on a large-scale, in depth and real time. This is the Finapp revolution: particle physics at the service of environmental and social sustainability.

Cosmic rays come from space and in contact with the Earth’s atmosphere generate a cascade of particles, including fast neutrons. The latter have the peculiarity of interacting mainly with water molecules. When they come into contact with water in the ground or snow, part of the fast neutrons is absorbed and part is reflected back into the air, losing part of the initial energy: thus slow neutrons are born. A large difference between the number of fast and slow neutrons implies a large amount of water and vice versa. Since fast neutrons have enough energy to penetrate inside the ground for many cm (meters in snow), the given figure is representative in depth. Since slow neutrons are distributed over large distances, it is possible to monitor the water content over vast areas, about 5 hectares at sea level.

entityDescription: NexWafe commercializes an innovative epitaxial silicon wafer production technology for advanced photovoltaic applications on Earth and in Space. Following a successful pilot, NexWafe is scaling toward commercial production at its 50 MW facility in Bitterfeld, Germany, focused on space wafers. Our proprietary EpiNex process grows ultra-thin, high-efficiency wafers directly on reusable seed wafers through high-throughput gas-to-wafer epitaxy. The newly produced wafer is detached while the seed wafer is recycled, replacing multiple conventional Czochralski steps and reducing energy use and CO₂ emissions by up to 60%, while cutting costs by 50%. As the only fully Western alternative to a market dominated (>99%) by China, NexWafe offers a secure, scalable, and cost-competitive solution to reshore photovoltaic supply chains to Europe. NexWafe’s staged scaling, from pilot to megawatt and gigawatt capacity, de-risks expansion to fulfill secured offtakes exceeding 9 GW, with initial production facility already oversubscribed. All offtakes are secured for the 1st commercial facility in Bitterfeld, including for the Space segment which brings >87% gross margin, making the facility profitable within the first year of operations. International scaling beyond Bitterfeld will be done in a capital-light licensing model, for which we already have a Strategic Partnership with Reliance Industries in India for at least a 6GW production. Our vision is to build a network of localized, economically sustainable wafer manufacturing across Europe and beyond, reinforcing Europe’s leadership in space value-chain manufacturing and supporting our energy independence through space.

HydroStar Europe (HydroStar) is a Green Hydrogen Technology Development Company. HydroStar designs and manufactures hardware that spans that the entire Hydrogen Value Chain including production, purification, compression, storage, and integration. HydroStar currently have 7 active hydrogen-related innovation projects as outlined below, (as of January 2025):

1x OFGEM Strategic Innovation Funding Beta Phase Project: Partnered with Wales and West Utilities, Welsh Water and Yeo Valley.
1x Clean Maritime Demonstration Competition 4: Partnered with Babcock International and London South Bank University
1x OFGEM NIA - Optimising Anaerobic Digestor Plants utilising Green Hydrogen: Partnered with Wales and West Utilities and Ixora Energy.
1x Hydrogen storage and distribution supply chain Collaborative R&D: Partnered with London South Bank University
1x Launchpad: net zero industry, South West Wales – R1 CR&D: Partnered with Cardiff University
1x UK-Australia Renewable Hydrogen Innovation Partnership Programme: Partnered with Northumbria University, UNSW, and Umax Ltd.
1x Smart Shipping - Renewable Hydrogen Mapping and Prospective Production: HydroStar only

HydroStar builds TRL9 Alkaline Electrolysers that are sized between 125kW and 1MW, but are also pioneering the design of membraneless electrolysers. These electrolysers are significantly cheaper than established PEM/Alkaline technology owing to the fact that there is no membrane and HydroStar only use stainless steel electrodes, as opposed to nafion and rare earth metals that are commonly. The lack of membrane also means that HydroStar are able to utilise impure water sources such as rainwater, grey water, final effluent and, seawater as an electrolyser feedstock unlike conventional technology that requires the use of water that has gone through the reverse osmosis (RO) process. This means that HydroStar produces hydrogen in line with stoichiometric values (9Litres of water per kg of H2 produced) whereas the RO process consumes anywhere from 9-15 Litres of potable water per Litre of Ultra Pure water produced.

HydroStar are also developing solid-state hydrogen storage technology (metal-hydrides) that are capable of storing hydrogen interstitially, but also can purify and compression hydrogen up to Grade D (99.97%) and 700bar respectively.This technology is considered the safest way to store hydrogen as it is chemically bonded to the metal alloy with no chance of escape unless the correct temperature and pressure conditions are met.

HydroStar is at the forefront of UK-based Green Hydrogen innovation and is striving for continued participation in sector-defining projects.

entityDescription:
Novac wants to enter the electric mobility market (both terrestrial and spatial), improving its efficiency and quality by means of supercapacitors, thus imposing a new quality standard for the best electric vehicles on the planet. The technology developed by Novac revolutionizes the supercapacitors market with two main characteristics: solid state and mouldability.

Supercapacitors are storage devices characterized by high specific power compared to traditional batteries; coupled to the normal batteries supplied, they would be used in situations where more power is needed, both in charge and discharge, guaranteeing better performance and life-cycle enhancement, having orders of magnitude longer life compared to batteries, and coupling them with batteries can improve the latter life as well, since a drastic stress reduction is achieved. This characteristic of supercaps assumes a very high value for aerospace applications, where long life-cycle and reliability are key factors.
Although the advantages of supercapacitors are clear and evident, at present there is little use of them due to the characteristics of the ones currently on the market. In fact, unlike Novac’s product, they are in a liquid state, containing flammable materials inside them, making them dangerous. Furthermore, these are supercapacitors of bulky and non-customizable dimensions, which makes it difficult to allow their application inside cars or space objects, and impossible inside scooters and bicycles. It is precisely these properties of the currently available supercapacitors that represent a great market opportunity for Novac, which with its own technology aims to revolutionize electric mobility by coupling batteries with safe, shape-customizable and high power density systems. By creating a much safer and liquid-free device, Novac’s product finds a perfect match with spatial applications, where the harsh working conditions impose limitations on the use of classic liquid state devices, making Novac unique on the market, also in terms of volume saving.

The SWE research group has strong expertise in space weather. More than 50 peer reviewed papers related to the Sun-Earth interaction guarantee the experience acquired in the framework of both national and international projects. Not only improving scientific knowledge on the Solar-Terrestrial interaction is the main goal for SWE, but also the development of space weather products, where the research group has proven experience in leading the Spanish Space Weather Service (http://www.senmes.es/) and providing products to the ESA SSA SWE Network (http://swe.ssa.esa.int/) through the Geomagnetism-Expert Centre. We also operate and maintain the Space Weather Station at the University of Alcala.
Regarding ESA activities, the SWE-UAH group has led two ESA contracts:
P3-SWE-XXXVII, SWE Products for Southern Europe - Phase 1, and
P3-SWE-XXIII, Space Weather User Needs for the Mediterranean Region. Now we are part of the consortium led by the Royal Belgian Institute for Space Aeronomy in the contract S2P - S1-SW-02.2, S1-SW-05, S1-SW-06 - Space Weather Service Network Development and Pre-Operation Part. All the previous contracts demonstrate the experience of the team in validating space weather products and implementing them in the ESA Portal through the SSO system. Users’ campaign to get feedback of our products were also developed in the framework of these contracts.
The SWE group has also participated in the ESA contract Synergetic use of SMOS L1 Data in Sun Flare detection and analysis, which allow us to propose the SMOS Mission for Space Weather Operations, considering the potential of near real-time solar observation at 1.4 GHz from MIRAS instrument.
